key_insight: MMControl introduces unified multi-modal control for joint audio–video diffusion models, letting users condition both audio and video simultaneously and improving cross-modal synchronization and alignment.
problem_solved: Existing controllable generation frameworks focus on video-only controls, limiting user control and often producing suboptimal audio–video alignment in joint generation models.
method: Extend joint audio–video Diffusion Transformer (DiT) models with modular control adapters that accept diverse control signals (e.g., motion sketches, audio cues, text).
Fuse modalities via dedicated cross-modal fusion layers and alignment objectives to enforce synchronized audio–video generation.
Provide a unified conditioning interface that composes multiple control sources into the diffusion sampling process for coherent joint outputs.
impact: Enables richer, user-driven creation and editing of synchronized audio–video content and advances research into controllable multimodal generative models—useful for media production, virtual agents, and multimodal research.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multiple control inputs (icons for text, audio waveform, motion sketch) → MMControl modules → joint audio+video output.
Component block: control adapters, cross-modal fusion, diffusion sampler, showing data flow and conditioning.
Before/after examples: uncontrolled vs. multi-controlled outputs highlighting improved audio–video sync.
Alignment visualization: timeline showing audio waveform aligned to key video frames to illustrate synchronization improvements.
paper_title: MMControl: Unified Multi-Modal Control for Joint Audio-Video Generation
paper_authors: Liyang Li, Wen Wang, Canyu Zhao, Tianjian Feng, Zhiyue Zhao
